sanskrit: samāhitaṃ pare tattve kṣīṇakāmam avasthitam sarvataḥ sukham anveti vapuś cāndramasaṃ yathā
english: To the one who is fixed upon the supreme truth, established in it, his desires worn away, happiness comes from every side, as light suffuses the orb of the moon.

sanskrit: saviśeṣāṇi bhūtāni guṇāṃś cābhajato muneḥ sukhenāpohyate duḥkhaṃ bhāskareṇa tamo yathā
english: For the sage who no longer cleaves to creatures with their distinctions, nor to the qualities, sorrow is driven off by happiness, as darkness is driven off by the sun.

sanskrit: tam atikrāntakarmāṇam atikrāntaguṇakṣayam brāhmaṇaṃ viṣayāśliṣṭaṃ jarāmṛtyū na vindataḥ
english: That brāhmaṇa who has passed beyond action, passed beyond the wasting of the qualities, and clings to no object of sense — old age and death do not find him.

sanskrit: sa yadā sarvato muktaḥ samaḥ paryavatiṣṭhate indriyāṇīndriyārthāṃś ca śarīrastho 'tivartate
english: When, freed on every side, he abides in perfect equanimity, then, though seated in the body, he transcends the senses and their objects.

sanskrit: kāraṇaṃ paramaṃ prāpya atikrāntasya kāryatām punarāvartanaṃ nāsti saṃprāptasya parāt param
english: Having attained the supreme Cause, having passed beyond all that is effect — for him who has reached the highest beyond the high, there is no returning again.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca dvaṃdvāni mokṣajijñāsur arthadharmāv anuṣṭhitaḥ vaktrā guṇavatā śiṣyaḥ śrāvyaḥ pūrvam idaṃ mahat
english: Vyāsa said: The disciple who would know liberation, who has practiced the pairs of opposites and observed both worldly gain and dharma, must first be made to hear this great teaching from a worthy preceptor.

sanskrit: ākāśaṃ māruto jyotir āpaḥ pṛthvī ca pañcamī bhāvābhāvau ca kālaś ca sarvabhūteṣu pañcasu
english: Ether, wind, fire, water, and earth the fifth — together with being and non-being, and time — these abide within all the five elements.

sanskrit: antarātmakam ākāśaṃ tanmayaṃ śrotram indriyam tasya śabdaṃ guṇaṃ vidyān mūrtiśāstravidhānavit
english: Ether is innermost in nature, and the ear, the organ of hearing, is made of it; one versed in the science and ordinance of embodied forms should know sound to be its quality.

sanskrit: caraṇaṃ mārutātmeti prāṇāpānau ca tanmayau sparśanaṃ cendriyaṃ vidyāt tathā sparśaṃ ca tanmayam
english: Motion is of the nature of wind, and the in-breath and out-breath are made of it; one should know that the organ of touch, and touch itself, are likewise made of it.

sanskrit: tataḥ pākaḥ prakāśaś ca jyotiś cakṣuś ca tanmayam tasya rūpaṃ guṇaṃ vidyān tamo 'nvavasitātmakam
english: From fire come digestion and light; the eye too is made of it, and its quality is known to be form — that which dispels the darkness inherent in things.

sanskrit: prakledaḥ kṣudratā sneha ity āpo hy upadiśyate rasanaṃ cendriyaṃ jihvā rasaś cāpāṃ guṇo mataḥ
english: Moistening, fineness, and fluid coherence are taught to be of water; the tongue is the organ of taste, and taste is held to be the quality of water.

sanskrit: saṃghātaḥ pārthivo dhātur asthidantanakhāni ca śmaśru loma ca keśāś ca sirāḥ snāyu ca carma ca
english: Solid mass is the earthen element: bones, teeth, and nails, beard, body-hair and the hair of the head, veins, sinews, and skin.

sanskrit: indriyaṃ ghrāṇasaṃjñānaṃ nāsikety abhidhīyate gandhaś caivendriyārtho 'yaṃ vijñeyaḥ pṛthivīmayaḥ
english: The organ that perceives by smelling is named the nose; and its object, odor, is to be known as made of earth.

sanskrit: uttareṣu guṇāḥ santi sarve sarveṣu cottarāḥ pañcānāṃ bhūtasaṃghānāṃ saṃtatiṃ munayo viduḥ
english: In the later elements all the qualities of the former are present, and the qualities of the later in all — thus the sages understand the unbroken sequence of the five elemental aggregates.

sanskrit: mano navamam eṣāṃ tu buddhis tu daśamī smṛtā ekādaśo 'ntarātmā ca sarvataḥ para ucyate
english: Among these the mind is the ninth, and the intellect is reckoned the tenth; the inner Self is the eleventh, and is declared to be supreme over all.

sanskrit: vyavasāyātmikā buddhir mano vyākaraṇātmakam karmānumānād vijñeyaḥ sa jīvaḥ kṣetrasaṃjñakaḥ
english: The intellect is of the nature of resolve, the mind of the nature of discrimination; from the inference of its action that living self, called the knower of the field, is to be known.

sanskrit: ebhiḥ kālāṣṭamair bhāvair yaḥ sarvaiḥ sarvam anvitam paśyaty akaluṣaṃ prājñaḥ sa mohaṃ nānuvartate
english: The wise one who, with all these principles — the elements together with time as the eighth — sees everything as pervaded by them, undimmed, does not fall prey to delusion.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca śarīrād vipramuktaṃ hi sūkṣmabhūtaṃ śarīriṇam karmabhiḥ paripaśyanti śāstroktaiḥ śāstracetasaḥ
english: Vyāsa said: The embodied self, become subtle and wholly released from the body — those whose minds are steeped in scripture perceive it fully through the disciplines the scriptures enjoin.

sanskrit: yathā marīcyaḥ sahitāś caranti; gacchanti tiṣṭhanti ca dṛśyamānāḥ dehair vimuktā vicaranti lokāṃs; tathaiva sattvāny atimānuṣāṇi
english: As rays of light move together, are seen to go and to stand still, so do beings beyond the human, released from their bodies, roam through the worlds.

sanskrit: pratirūpaṃ yathaivāpsu tāpaḥ sūryasya lakṣyate sattvavāṃs tu tathā sattvaṃ pratirūpaṃ prapaśyati
english: As the heat of the sun is seen reflected as an image upon the waters, so does the one endowed with the pure essence behold that essence as a reflected likeness.

sanskrit: tāni sūkṣmāṇi sattvasthā vimuktāni śarīrataḥ svena tattvena tattvajñāḥ paśyanti niyatendriyāḥ
english: Those subtle beings, freed from the body and abiding in pure essence, the knowers of truth, their senses controlled, behold by their own true insight.

sanskrit: svapatāṃ jāgratāṃ caiva sarveṣām ātmacintitam pradhānadvaidhayuktānāṃ jahatāṃ karmajaṃ rajaḥ
english: Whether men sleep or wake, the Self is what all of them ponder — those joined to the duality of primal Nature, who cast off the passion born of works.

sanskrit: yathāhani tathā rātrau yathā rātrau tathāhani vaśe tiṣṭhati sattvātmā satataṃ yogayoginām
english: As by day, so by night; as by night, so by day — the essential Self stands ever in the mastery of those who are steadfast in yoga.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ nityaṃ sadānityo bhūtātmā satataṃ guṇaiḥ saptabhis tv anvitaḥ sūkṣmaiś cariṣṇur ajarāmaraḥ
english: In them the elemental self, though ever transient, is yet eternal; endowed always with the seven subtle qualities, it wanders on, unaging and undying.

sanskrit: manobuddhiparābhūtaḥ svadehaparadehavit svapneṣv api bhavaty eṣa vijñātā sukhaduḥkhayoḥ
english: Surpassing mind and intellect, knowing both its own body and others' bodies, even in dreams it remains the one who experiences pleasure and pain.

sanskrit: tatrāpi labhate duḥkhaṃ tatrāpi labhate sukham krodhalobhau tu tatrāpi kṛtvā vyasanam archati
english: There too it meets with sorrow, there too it meets with joy; there too, giving way to anger and greed, it comes to misfortune.

sanskrit: prīṇitaś cāpi bhavati mahato 'rthān avāpya ca karoti puṇyaṃ tatrāpi jāgrann iva ca paśyati
english: It is gladdened too, on gaining great wealth, and there too it performs meritorious deeds; and it sees, even there, as though awake.

sanskrit: tam evam atitejoṃśaṃ bhūtātmānaṃ hṛdi sthitam tamorajobhyām āviṣṭā nānupaśyanti mūrtiṣu
english: This elemental self, with its portion of surpassing radiance, seated within the heart — those overcome by darkness and passion do not perceive it in embodied forms.

sanskrit: śāstrayogaparā bhūtvā svam ātmānaṃ parīpsavaḥ anucchvāsāny amūrtīni yāni vajropamāny api
english: Becoming devoted to scripture and yoga, longing to grasp their own Self — those things that are breathless and formless, yet hard as the thunderbolt —

sanskrit: pṛthagbhūteṣu sṛṣṭeṣu caturṣv āśramakarmasu samādhau yogam evaitac chāṇḍilyaḥ śamam abravīt
english: Among the four separately ordained orders of life and their duties, Śāṇḍilya declared this very yoga, in deep meditation, to be the path of inner peace.

sanskrit: viditvā sapta sūkṣmāṇi ṣaḍaṅgaṃ ca maheśvaram pradhānaviniyogasthaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati
english: Having known the seven subtle principles and the six-membered Great Lord, established in the right ordering of primal Nature, one attains the supreme Brahman.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca hṛdi kāmadrumaś citro mohasaṃcayasaṃbhavaḥ krodhamānamahāskandho vivitsāparimocanaḥ
english: Vyāsa said: In the heart stands the wondrous tree of desire, sprung from the accumulation of delusion, its great trunk anger and pride, never letting go its craving to possess.

sanskrit: tasya cājñānam ādhāraḥ pramādaḥ pariṣecanam so 'bhyasūyāpalāśo hi purāduṣkṛtasāravān
english: Its support is ignorance, its watering is heedlessness; its foliage is envy, and its sap is the evil done in former times.

sanskrit: saṃmohacintāviṭapaḥ śokaśākho bhayaṃkaraḥ mohanībhiḥ pipāsābhir latābhiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ
english: Its boughs are confusion and anxious care, its branches grief; terrible to behold, it is wrapped about with creepers of bewildering thirst.

sanskrit: upāsate mahāvṛkṣaṃ sulubdhās taṃ phalepsavaḥ āyāsaiḥ saṃyataḥ pāśaiḥ phalāni pariveṣṭayan
english: The greedy, longing for its fruit, wait upon that great tree, bound fast by toilsome snares as they wrap themselves around its fruits.

sanskrit: yas tān pāśān vaśe kṛtvā taṃ vṛkṣam apakarṣati gataḥ sa duḥkhayor antaṃ yatamānas tayor dvayoḥ
english: He who, mastering those snares, tears that tree away, striving against the pair of them, reaches the end of both sorrows.

sanskrit: saṃrohaty akṛtaprajñaḥ saṃtāpena hi pādapam sa tam eva tato hanti viṣaṃ grastam ivāturam
english: The man of unripe wisdom makes the tree grow again through his own torment, and so it destroys him, as poison destroys the sick man who has swallowed it.

sanskrit: tasyānuśayamūlasya mūlam uddhriyate balāt tyāgāpramādākṛtinā sāmyena paramāsinā
english: The root of that tree, whose root is lingering attachment, is torn up by force with the supreme sword of equanimity, wrought of renunciation and vigilance.

sanskrit: evaṃ yo veda kāmasya kevalaṃ parikarṣaṇam vadhaṃ vai kāmaśāstrasya sa duḥkhāny ativartate
english: He who thus knows how utterly desire may be uprooted, and the slaying of the science of desire, passes beyond all sorrows.

sanskrit: śarīraṃ puram ity āhuḥ svāminī buddhir iṣyate tatra buddheḥ śarīrasthaṃ mano nāmārthacintakam
english: The body, they say, is a city, and the intellect is held to be its mistress; within it, seated in the body, subject to the intellect, is the mind, the contemplator of objects.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi janāḥ paurās tadarthaṃ tu parā kṛtiḥ tatra dvau dāruṇau doṣau tamo nāma rajas tathā
english: The senses are the townsfolk, the citizens; and the higher faculty exists for their sake. There dwell two cruel faults, the one named darkness, the other passion.

sanskrit: yadartham upajīvanti paurāḥ sahapureśvarāḥ advāreṇa tam evārthaṃ dvau doṣāv upajīvataḥ
english: That very good by which the citizens, together with the lord of the city, sustain themselves — by an unlawful gate those two faults feed upon it.

sanskrit: tatra buddhir hi durdharṣā manaḥ sādharmyam ucyate paurāś cāpi manas trastās teṣām api calā sthitiḥ
english: There the intellect is hard to assail; the mind is said to be of like nature with it. The citizens too are in awe of the mind, and their footing also is unsteady.

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ buddhir adhyāste na so 'rthaḥ pariṣīdati yadarthaṃ pṛthag adhyāste manas tat pariṣīdati
english: The aim upon which the intellect settles does not perish; but the aim upon which the mind settles apart, by itself, that does perish.

sanskrit: pṛthagbhūtaṃ yadā buddhyā mano bhavati kevalam tatrainaṃ vivṛtaṃ śūnyaṃ rajaḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
english: When the mind becomes severed from the intellect and stands alone, then passion takes its stand upon it, finding it exposed and empty.

sanskrit: tan manaḥ kurute sakhyaṃ rajasā saha saṃgatam taṃ cādāya janaṃ pauraṃ rajase saṃprayacchati
english: That mind, having joined with passion, makes friendship with it, and taking the people, the citizens, it delivers them over to passion.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca bhūtānāṃ guṇasaṃkhyānaṃ bhūyaḥ putra niśāmaya dvaipāyanamukhād bhraṣṭaṃ ślāghayā parayānagha
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear once more, my son, the enumeration of the qualities of the elements, fallen from the mouth of Dvaipāyana with high praise, O sinless one.

sanskrit: dīptānalanibhaḥ prāha bhagavān dhūmravarcase tato 'ham api vakṣyāmi bhūyaḥ putra nidarśanam
english: Like a blazing fire, the venerable one spoke it to Dhūmravarcas; and so I too, my son, shall set forth this teaching again as an illustration.

sanskrit: bhūmeḥ sthairyaṃ pṛthutvaṃ ca kāṭhinyaṃ prasavātmatā gandho gurutvaṃ śaktiś ca saṃghātaḥ sthāpanā dhṛtiḥ
english: Of earth: steadfastness, extension, hardness, the power of bringing forth, odor, heaviness, strength, cohesion, the holding of things in place, and firmness.

sanskrit: apāṃ śaityaṃ rasaḥ kledo dravatvaṃ snehasaumyatā jihvā viṣyandinī caiva bhaumāpyāsravaṇaṃ tathā
english: Of water: coldness, taste, moisture, fluidity, soft unctuousness, the flowing tongue, and the trickling forth of the watery within the earthen.

sanskrit: agner durdharṣatā tejas tāpaḥ pākaḥ prakāśanam śaucaṃ rāgo laghus taikṣṇyaṃ daśamaṃ cordhvabhāgitā
english: Of fire: unassailability, brilliance, heat, the power to cook, illumination, purity, color, lightness, sharpness, and tenth, the tendency to move upward.

sanskrit: vāyor aniyamaḥ sparśo vādasthānaṃ svatantratā balaṃ śaighryaṃ ca mohaś ca ceṣṭā karmakṛtā bhavaḥ
english: Of wind: unrestraint, touch, the seat of speech, independence, strength, swiftness, the power to bewilder, activity, the doing of work, and becoming.

sanskrit: ākāśasya guṇaḥ śabdo vyāpitvaṃ chidratāpi ca anāśrayam anālambam avyaktam avikāritā
english: The qualities of ether are sound, pervasiveness, and porousness; it is without support, without resting-place, unmanifest, and free from change.

sanskrit: apratīghātatā caiva bhūtatvaṃ vikṛtāni ca guṇāḥ pañcāśataṃ proktāḥ pañcabhūtātmabhāvitāḥ
english: Together with imperviousness, elemental being, and its modifications — these are declared to be the fifty qualities, brought into being from the nature of the five elements.

sanskrit: calopapattir vyaktiś ca visargaḥ kalpanā kṣamā sad asac cāśutā caiva manaso nava vai guṇāḥ
english: Restless arising, manifestation, projection, imagination, forbearance, the real and the unreal, and swiftness — these are the nine qualities of the mind.

sanskrit: iṣṭāniṣṭavikalpaś ca vyavasāyaḥ samādhitā saṃśayaḥ pratipattiś ca buddhau pañceha ye guṇāḥ
english: The choosing between the welcome and the unwelcome, resolve, concentration, doubt, and ascertainment — these are the five qualities that reside in the intellect.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ pañcaguṇā buddhiḥ kathaṃ pañcendriyā guṇāḥ etan me sarvam ācakṣva sūkṣmajñānaṃ pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How does the intellect have five qualities? How are the qualities of the nature of the five senses? Explain all this to me, this subtle knowledge, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca āhuḥ ṣaṣṭiṃ bhūtaguṇān vai; bhūtaviśiṣṭā nityaviṣaktāḥ bhūtaviṣaktāś cākṣarasṛṣṭāḥ; putra na nityaṃ tad iha vadanti
english: Bhīṣma said: They speak of sixty qualities of the elements — distinct from the elements yet ever clinging to them, clinging to the elements yet sprung from the Imperishable; and this, my son, they declare to be not eternal here.

sanskrit: tat putra cintākalitaṃ yad uktam; anāgataṃ vai tava saṃpratīha bhūtārthatattvaṃ tad avāpya sarvaṃ; bhūtaprabhāvād bhava śāntabuddhiḥ
english: This, my son, framed by reflection, has been told you — what was not yet known to you is now made present here. Having grasped the whole truth of the elements and their meaning, become, through understanding the power of the elements, one of tranquil mind.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ya ime pṛthivīpālāḥ śerate pṛthivītale pṛtanāmadhya ete hi gatasattvā mahābalāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: These guardians of the earth who lie upon the earth's surface — these mighty ones, fallen amid their armies, their life-breath gone —

sanskrit: ekaikaśo bhīmabalā nāgāyutabalās tathā ete hi nihatāḥ saṃkhye tulyatejobalair naraiḥ
english: Each one of fearful strength, strong as ten thousand elephants — these were struck down in battle by men of strength and splendor equal to their own.

sanskrit: naiṣāṃ paśyāmi hantāraṃ prāṇināṃ saṃyuge purā vikrameṇopasaṃpannās tejobalasamanvitāḥ
english: I do not see who, in the battle long ago, could have been the slayer of these living men, endowed as they were with valor and possessed of splendor and strength.

sanskrit: atha ceme mahāprājña śerate hi gatāsavaḥ mṛtā iti ca śabdo 'yaṃ vartaty eṣu gatāsuṣu
english: And yet, O greatly wise one, here they lie with their breath departed, and this word 'dead' is used of them whose life has fled.

sanskrit: ime mṛtā nṛpatayaḥ prāyaśo bhīmavikramāḥ tatra me saṃśayo jātaḥ kutaḥ saṃjñā mṛtā iti
english: These dead kings were for the most part of terrible prowess; and a doubt has arisen in me — whence comes this name, 'the dead'?

sanskrit: kasya mṛtyuḥ kuto mṛtyuḥ kena mṛtyur iha prajāḥ haraty amarasaṃkāśa tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Whose is death, whence is death, by what means does death carry off creatures here? O you who are like a god immortal, tell me this, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca purā kṛtayuge tāta rājāsīd avikampakaḥ sa śatruvaśam āpannaḥ saṃgrāme kṣīṇavāhanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Long ago, in the Kṛta age, my child, there lived a king named Avikampaka; in battle, his forces wasted away, he fell into the power of his foes.

sanskrit: tatra putro harir nāma nārāyaṇasamo bale sa śatrubhir hataḥ saṃkhye sabalaḥ sapadānugaḥ
english: His son was named Hari, equal in strength to Nārāyaṇa; he was slain in the fray by the enemy, together with his army and his followers.

sanskrit: sa rājā śatruvaśagaḥ putraśokasamanvitaḥ yadṛcchayāśāntiparo dadarśa bhuvi nāradam
english: That king, fallen into the enemy's power and overwhelmed with grief for his son, finding no peace, beheld by chance the sage Nārada upon the earth.

sanskrit: sa tasmai sarvam ācaṣṭa yathā vṛttaṃ janeśvaraḥ śatrubhir grahaṇaṃ saṃkhye putrasya maraṇaṃ tathā
english: To him the lord of men told all that had befallen — his capture by the enemy in battle, and likewise the death of his son.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā nārado 'tha tapodhanaḥ ākhyānam idam ācaṣṭa putraśokāpahaṃ tadā
english: Hearing those words of his, Nārada, rich in austerities, then related this tale, which takes away grief for a son.

sanskrit: rājañ śṛṇu samākhyānam adyedaṃ bahuvistaram yathā vṛttaṃ śrutaṃ caiva mayāpi vasudhādhipa
english: O king, hear now this story, full and far-ranging, even as it came to pass and as it was heard by me, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā mahātejāḥ prajāsarge pitāmahaḥ atīva vṛddhā bahulā nāmṛṣyata punaḥ prajāḥ
english: When in the creation of beings the great and mighty Grandsire had brought forth his creatures, those creatures, grown exceedingly numerous, he could no longer endure.

sanskrit: na hy antaram abhūt kiṃ cit kva cij jantubhir acyuta nirucchvāsam ivonnaddhaṃ trailokyam abhavan nṛpa
english: For there was no space anywhere at all left free of living things, O imperishable one; the three worlds, so crammed, became as if unable to breathe, O king.

sanskrit: tasya cintā samutpannā saṃhāraṃ prati bhūpate cintayan nādhyagacchac ca saṃhāre hetukāraṇam
english: Then anxious thought arose in him concerning their destruction, O ruler of the earth; yet pondering, he could not find the cause and means for their destruction.

sanskrit: tasya roṣān mahārāja khebhyo 'gnir udatiṣṭhata tena sarvā diśo rājan dadāha sa pitāmahaḥ
english: From his wrath, O great king, a fire arose out of his bodily apertures, and with it the Grandsire set ablaze all the quarters of the sky.

sanskrit: tato divaṃ bhuvaṃ khaṃ ca jagac ca sacarācaram dadāha pāvako rājan bhagavatkopasaṃbhavaḥ
english: Then heaven, earth, and the firmament, and the whole world with all that moves and stands still, that fire, born of the Lord's anger, consumed, O king.

sanskrit: tatrādahyanta bhūtāni jaṅgamāni dhruvāṇi ca mahatā kopavegena kupite prapitāmahe
english: There were beings burned, both moving and unmoving alike, by that mighty surge of wrath, when the great Grandsire was enraged.

sanskrit: tato harijaṭaḥ sthāṇur vedādhvarapatiḥ śivaḥ jagāda śaraṇaṃ devo brahmāṇaṃ paravīrahā
english: Then Sthāṇu, the tawny-matted one, lord of the Vedas and of sacrifice, the auspicious god Śiva, slayer of enemy heroes, went to Brahmā for refuge.

sanskrit: tasminn abhigate sthāṇau prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā abravīd varado devo jvalann iva tadā śivam
english: When Sthāṇu had thus come, out of his desire for the welfare of creatures, the boon-granting god, blazing as it were, spoke then to Śiva:

sanskrit: karavāṇy adya kaṃ kāmaṃ varārho 'si mato mama kartā hy asmi priyaṃ śambho tava yad dhṛdi vartate
english: What wish shall I fulfill for you today? You are deemed by me worthy of a boon. For I shall do whatever pleases you, O Śambhu, whatever lies within your heart.
